To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the pupils’ and teachers’ perceptions on the constructivist and instructive climate in 4th-6th grades of primary school in the Republic of Macedonia are positive and they are in accordance with each other.
the pupils and teachers in the 4th, the 5th and the 6th grade of compulsory school have a similar opinion on the class climate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the perceptions of pupils and teachers on class climate in 4th to 6th grades in compulsory school.
class climate, its components and its impact on the learning achievement of pupils in the 4th,5th and 6th grades at the compulsory school.
pupils’ and teachers’ perceptions of the constructivist climate in 4th-6th grades of elementary school.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pupils and the teachers have a positive attitude towards class climate in the 4th, the 5th and the 6th grade of compulsory education.
the pupils and teachers perceptions of class climate are in general positive, but there is still a lot of room to work on in the direction of improving the class climate.

in 4th grade, 5th grade, 6th grade of compulsory school, in the majority of classes, predominates positive constructivistic class climate, inclusive and cooperative, but there are also instructive class climates where the teacher is at the center and where pupils are a little involved in the restructuring of knowledge, skills or attitudes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pupils and teachers in 4th and 5th grades of elementary school have a positive perception of their class climate, while the pupils in the 6th grade perceive their class climate as negative.
the constructivist climate is more often perceived by pupils than teachers and that the pupils’ perception of the climate in their classes is more positive.
the pupils’ perceptions of the class climate are in line with the teachers’ perceptions, but the differences between them are also evident, especially regarding the constructivist climate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a strong need to develop a better understanding of how teachers and students perceive class climate and how these perceptions influence the learning process.
the classroom climate is a complex construct that is influenced by many different factors.
the teacher’s perception of the classroom climate is more important than the student’s perception of the climate.
